chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), that he said:

Regarding the woman who menstruates once every three months, or in six months, or in seven months; and the istihadah (continuous bleeding) woman who has not reached the age of menstruation; and the woman who menstruates once and then stops once; and the woman who has no hope of bearing children; and the woman whose menstruation has stopped but she claims she has not despaired (of menopause); and the woman who sees yellowish discharge from menstruation which is not regular. He mentioned that the waiting period (iddah) of all of these is three months.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a woman with irregular menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the specific legal category of 'muhtadid' (women with irregular menstruation), including those with extended cycles or pre-menopausal bleeding, establishing a uniform three-month waiting period (iddah) for them. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it provides a clear, practical solution for women whose biological signs do not fit the standard monthly cycle, ensuring legal certainty in matters of marriage and inheritance. The text highlights the scholarly approach of grouping diverse physiological conditions under a single, manageable legal framework based on the Prophet's or Imams' guidance.
